solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son accompanying president around Brown and another US university

indicators.note: the son and president go around the brown colour, enclosing it

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US president
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A student and a US president visit one American university and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container. Brown is itself an Ivy League university, which is why the definition says 'another US university'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanford is a leading private university in California, so it is another American seat of learning.

clue.text: Doctor likes gripping cold cutting implement

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grip the cold letter, holding it inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A doctor fancies a sharp blade he is holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges LIKES, and 'gripping' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved blade used for cutting grain or grass.

clue.text: Records of former Indian currency oddly lost

parts.note: the anna was a coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Records of an old Indian coin have strangely gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of 'lost', L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records kept year by year.

clue.text: Substantial weight put on a religious ruling

parts.note: fat means substantial, as in a fat fee

explanation.surface: A cleric issues a heavy ruling on someone who has gained weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a ruling on Islamic law given by a recognised authority.

clue.text: Comedian's act is run-of-the-mill

definitions.meaning: a comic's set piece of material

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a comic's turn as ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine is both a rehearsed performance and an adjective for something humdrum.

clue.text: Something done one's seen in part of London

indicators.note: the numeral is seen within the district's name, placed inside it

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is short for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a deed has been witnessed somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a deed, a thing someone has done.

clue.text: Bird, fish and insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A list of three creatures: a bird, a fish and a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a common scavenging insect.

clue.text: A fan of any anthem from time to time, say

parts.note: to be into something is to be a fan of it

indicators.note: occasionally, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fan of anthems who listens now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the even letters of 'any anthem', NATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To intonate is to utter or recite, especially in a chanting tone.

clue.text: A number want sandwiches trimmed

indicators.note: the outer word sandwiches the rest, enclosing it like bread

parts.note: to want is to need
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Several people want sandwiches with the crusts cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' is the container signal, not food: the outer word holds the rest like bread round a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatened means tidied up, as trimmed hair or a hedge is.

clue.text: Interpret negative things honestly

parts.note: cons are the drawbacks, as in pros and cons
true as an adverb, as in 'speak true', means honestly

explanation.surface: Someone is told to read the drawbacks in good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a statement is to work out or explain its meaning.

clue.text: Reserve empty table with a drink

parts.note: ice means reserve, a cool formal manner

indicators.note: an empty word loses its contents, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone books a table, finds it bare, and orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the ends of 'table', TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled beverage, and ice tea is a common variant of the name.

clue.text: Rider on way over here!

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript, PS
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cyclist on the road is called over.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the sound made to attract someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Gentle songs calm small kids, though not at first

parts.note: to lull is to calm or soothe

indicators.note: the word for the kids loses its opening letter

parts.note: babies are small children

explanation.surface: Soft songs settle young children, though they did not work at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not at first' takes the B off BABIES, leaving ABIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lullabies are soothing songs sung to send a child to sleep.

clue.text: Series of mountains — get hot cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to get hot under the collar is to anger; anger is the heat of temper

explanation.surface: Hikers overheat while biking through a mountain chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final R of ANGER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or chain of mountains.

clue.text: He's a smashing sporting legend

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words up so their letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan praises a sportsman as a smashing great of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe was an American tennis champion, so 'smashing' doubles as a tennis smash.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe won Wimbledon in 1975 and is a celebrated figure in tennis history.

clue.text: Truthfulness occasionally heard in Vegas, for example

indicators.note: the selected letters go in the city nickname

parts.note: Las Vegas is nicknamed Sin City

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone claims honesty is rarely heard in Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes E and R from 'heard', placed inside SIN CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincerity is the quality of being genuine and honest.

clue.text: Snack and wine consumed by one on foot

indicators.note: the wine is swallowed up inside the digit, enclosed by it

parts.note: a toe is one of the digits on a foot
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A hiker eats a snack and drinks wine on the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a light bite or snack.

clue.text: European playwright succeeded with horror story

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a chiller is a frightening tale

explanation.surface: A dramatist from Europe made a hit with a scary tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German dramatist, author of Mary Stuart and William Tell.

clue.text: Foremost clinical reason for a runny nose?

parts.note: head means foremost, as in head waiter
clinical means detached and unemotional, that is, cold

explanation.surface: A doctor's leading diagnosis for a streaming nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold is a viral infection whose main symptom is a blocked or runny nose.

clue.text: Having taken drug, groups of people head for emergency detox

indicators.note: the groups take in the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: clans are groups of related families
E is short for ecstasy

indicators.note: head for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Groups of people who took drugs go to A&E to dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having taken' puts E inside CLANS, making CLEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse the body is to rid it of toxins, the verb sense of detox.

clue.text: Language coming from overseas

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A tongue that came from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic.

clue.text: Hospital in very old district of New York

indicators.note: the hospital letter sits in the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital stands in a very old part of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: SoHo is a Manhattan neighbourhood, named from 'South of Houston Street'.

clue.text: Kerry's good health entails exercising

indicators.note: exercising works the letters about into new positions

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: staying healthy in Kerry involves working out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerry is a county in Ireland, so this is the Irish toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slainte is the Gaelic toast meaning health, raised in Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Extremely zeitgeisty type of art and dance music

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: Art Deco is a style of art and design

explanation.surface: A trendy blend of art style and dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is the accordion-led dance music of Louisiana Creoles.

clue.text: Car in ultimately unusable condition

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A car ends up in a state where it cannot be driven.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a car with an extended rear cargo area.

clue.text: Popular source of documentaries that is not mainstream

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A popular supplier of documentaries is an independent outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie describes independent music, film or publishing outside the big commercial labels.

clue.text: Ones with bones?

parts.note: bones is slang for dice, so this means two ones shown on a pair of dice

explanation.surface: A question about creatures that have skeletons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bones' is old slang for dice, and the throw of a one on each die has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake eyes is the craps term for rolling a pair of ones with two dice.

clue.text: I am upset to be included in the Spanish messages online

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is upset to be copied into Spanish internet messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is electronic mail, the messages sent over the internet.

clue.text: Opportunity, yes, to cut some meat

indicators.note: the word for yes cuts into the meat, sitting within it

parts.note: loin is a cut of meat
OK means yes

explanation.surface: A butcher is given the nod to carve some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is a chance to take part, as in 'never got a look-in'.

clue.text: American going to pieces behind closed doors

indicators.note: falling to bits suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A US citizen has a breakdown in private.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is the legal Latin phrase for a hearing held in private, away from the public.

clue.text: Change colours, perhaps, to hide electronic flaw in photo

indicators.note: the outer word conceals the letter by holding it inside

parts.note: to redye is to colour again, perhaps changing the shade
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A photographer recolours an image to cover up a technical fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the red glare in subjects' pupils caused by a camera flash.

clue.text: How steak may be good for you

explanation.surface: A diner is told how their steak is cooked and that it is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Well done is both a degree of cooking meat and an exclamation of congratulation.
